extracted.intended_audience: investigators and small business applicants preparing Phase II STTR (NIH/NIAID) grant applications, and institutional grant administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting a Phase II STTR grant application (PHS 2020-2 / PA-20-265) for development of small-molecule therapeutics, including required forms, research plan, resource/authentication plans, and compliance documentation. Emphasis on standards for experimental rigor, resource authentication, facilities, and data/resource sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow funding opportunity instructions for application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH/NIAID posts sample applications periodically; samples may not reflect latest format or rules. Use the FOA-specific instructions for required sections, order, and submission details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications and assurances; authorized representative signature
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing this application, I certify (1) to the statements contained in the list of certifications and (2) that the statements herein are true, complete and accurate to the best of my knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature attests to awareness of penalties for false statements (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001); the list of certifications/assurances is contained in the announcement or agency instructions and must be agreed to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required SF424 R&R and PHS-398 components
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must include standard SF424 R&R and PHS-398 components as listed (Cover Page, Project Summary/Abstract, Project Narrative, Facilities & Other Resources, Equipment, Senior/Key Personnel, Research & Related Budget(s), Budget Justification, Research Plan (Specific Aims, Research Strategy), Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information, Vertebrate Animals, Resource Sharing Plan(s), Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources, Bibliography & References Cited, Consortium/Contractual Arrangements, Letters of Support, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a detailed Table of Contents with page references; include all required attachments and organization information per FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects compliance and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether human subjects are involved; if yes, indicate exemption status, IRB review pending or approved, and provide Human Subject Assurance number where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not exempt, provide IRB approval or pending status; include Project Summary/Abstract and Project Narrative files, inclusion enrollment reports, consent processes, specimen labeling (coded), and protections for confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals compliance and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether vertebrate animals are used; if yes, indicate IACUC review pending or approved and provide Animal Welfare Assurance number where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide vertebrate animals sections describing animal use, welfare, and compliance with USDA/AAALAC/PHS policies; include IACUC approval dates when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary/privileged information and FOIA considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if proprietary/privileged information is included in the application. NIH will respond to FOIA requests subject to exemptions and may redact confidential commercial/financial information, reviewer comments, deliberations, and personal privacy information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark proprietary content appropriately; expect redactions under FOIA and protect confidential business information accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental and historic site impact disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether the project has an actual or potential impact (positive or negative) on the environment and whether the site is designated or eligible as a historic place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, provide explanations and indicate whether an environmental assessment (EA) or environmental impact statement (EIS) has been performed or exemption authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan and compliance with NIH public access/data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to rapidly sharing data following NIH guidelines; prepare and submit peer-reviewed publications to publicaccess@nih.gov within required timeframes; make project resources available per NIH policy and distribute materials to collaborators and requestors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After patent filing (if appropriate), prepare data for publication; fill material requests in a timely fashion; include specific Resource Sharing Plan attachments in application (e.g., data, model organisms, genomic data where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources must document environment and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed description of facilities, laboratory space, specialized equipment, core resources, and institutional environment that will support the proposed research (e.g., BSL-level labs, imaging cores, NMR, LC/MS, HPLCs, centrifuges, vivarium).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe square footage, BSL capabilities, shared instruments, administrative support, access to cores/cores at partner institutions, and how the environment contributes to project success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory notebook maintenance and records retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas, calculations and experimental results are entered into the notebook as soon as possible (preferably same date); all notebook pages are signed and dated by the researcher on a daily basis; entries are made in permanent ink without skipping pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notebooks are signed daily and witnessed monthly; notebooks kept locked when not in use; NMR data archived on a primary server and periodically downloaded to a backup server; standard industry confidentiality practices observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound identity, purity, registration, and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: New chemical entities and scale-ups will be synthesized using modern methods and established analyses for chemical identity and purity (e.g., ≥95% by 1H NMR and LC/MS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If purity <95% a management review occurs and apparent purity is indicated in comments; approved structures are entered into an electronic database with unique ID (Instant JChem), recorded in the lab notebook, stored refrigerated in well-marked vials in a locked compound repository; compounds prepared for one project are not cross-screened for different projects without original collaborator written consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of antibodies and characterization after storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticate antibodies upon receipt and when used after long storage (>6 months) by Western blot using cells overexpressing the antigen or cells with gene-specific silencing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide manufacturer specification sheets; maintain documentation of authentication and vendor/source; include antibody authentication steps in the Authentication of Key Biological Resources section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell line authentication and mycoplasma testing schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Cell lines will be purchased from ATCC or certified cores; lines obtained from ATCC have been authenticated by STR profiling; monitor for mycoplasma contamination every 10th passage or every 12 months, whichever comes first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document provenance (ATCC or core), STR profiles, and mycoplasma testing results; ensure cells used in experiments are authenticated and contamination-free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression plasmid authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticate all expression plasmids by direct sequencing; for subsequent amplifications and distributions verify identity by restriction digest and gel electrophoresis or direct DNA sequencing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain sequencing records and verification steps whenever constructs are amplified or shared with collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: CROs, vendors, and reagent authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek authentication of reagents, starting materials, antibodies, and biological results from reputable vendors via product specifications and work descriptions; independently verify if issues arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document vendor specifications and be prepared to confirm reagent identity/performance as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis plan and criteria for significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical evaluation: p-values less than 0.05 interpreted as statistically significant. Assess normality with probability plots and Shapiro-Wilks tests; non-normal data compared with Mann-Whitney U test; non-normal data may be log-transformed and reassessed; if normally distributed use F-test for equality of variance; if variance inequality use Welch's t-test; if homoscedastic use Student t-test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe normality checks, transformations, and which statistical tests will be used under which conditions; include plans for multiple comparisons and confirm assumptions prior to test selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental replication and sample size standards (rigor and reproducibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each virus infection experiment, perform ≥3 independent tests in triplicate. Experiments with human MDMs performed using ≥6 different healthy adult donors per year (50:50 female:male). In vivo studies to be repeated at least once and use ≥5 mice per experimental condition for both sexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect similar outcome trends among donors though magnitudes may vary; analyze data with appropriate tests (Student t-test for two groups or one-way ANOVA for >2 groups) and inspect for normality and apply transformations or non-parametric tests as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virus stock authentication, purification, titration, and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Virus stocks should be prepared/purified (e.g., ultracentrifugation through sucrose cushion), titered (report FFU or PFU per mL), confirmed mycoplasma- and endotoxin-free, deep-sequenced or PCR-sequenced to confirm identity and matched to NCBI accession numbers, and stored at appropriate ultra-low temperatures (e.g., ≤-65°C) in appropriate containment (e.g., ABSL4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document passage history, titers, sequencing results, and storage conditions; provide evidence of purity and identity for viruses used in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subject recruitment criteria and specimen handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Human subjects (for blood-derived macrophages) limited to normal healthy adult volunteers 18-50 years old; recruit to achieve 50% female:male ratio; obtain venous blood via venipuncture; label specimens with numerical codes to protect confidentiality; record date and amount of blood withdrawn in locked records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide IRB protocol reference, informed consent procedures, and specimen coding to maintain confidentiality; limit collection to specified donor characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mouse primary cell isolation and characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary peritoneal macrophages isolated from wild-type Balb/c mice using well-established published protocols; characterize isolated populations visually and by immunofluorescence for macrophage-specific markers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document isolation protocol, yields, purity, viability, and markers used for validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and procurement of antibodies, chemicals, siRNAs, PCR primers
rubrics_metrics.description: Select reagents based on published literature and purchase from reputable commercial vendors in sufficient quantities; if obtaining additional batches, purchase products with identical specifications from the same vendors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain vendor/product specifications and lot numbers; include plans for validation where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records retention and data backup for chemical and analytical data
rubrics_metrics.description: Final compound samples stored in a locked repository; laboratory notebooks signed daily and witnessed monthly; NMR spectral data archived on primary server and periodically copied to backup server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain electronic databases (e.g., Instant JChem), software licenses (e.g., SciFinder-n), and backup strategies to support patent filings and publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify biosafety level and biohazard approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the biosafety level required for the work (e.g., BSL-2 work described; ABSL4 repositories described for high containment viruses) and that work will be conducted under appropriate approved conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate that work involving BSL agents follows approved containment, institutional approvals, and that experiments are performed in appropriate BSL facilities with documented biosafety practices.
